title: Unify stop/logprobs semantics and stabilize incremental streaming for function/tool-call payloads
author: Samir Patel
description:
Motivation: Several customers and our OpenAI-compatibility tests uncovered mismatches in how /v1/chat.completions semantics are surfaced when using streaming + function/tool calling. Specifically: 1) `stop` handling differed between non-streaming and streaming code paths (arrays vs single-string edge cases), causing early termination or missing finish reasons; 2) `logprobs` were emitted incrementally in a way that clients interpreted as final probabilities (leaking unstable partial scores); 3) function/tool-calling deltas (partial 'arguments' emission) were not consistently shaped to match OpenAI streaming expectations, which broke a handful of client SDKs and led to flaky canaries. This PR unifies semantics and stabilizes the streaming emitter so OpenAI-compatible clients see consistent, production-grade behavior.

Summary of changes:
- Normalize `stop` parameter parsing at the API boundary so both string and array forms are treated identically for streaming and non-streaming flows; add deterministic trimming behavior when a stop sequence spans a token boundary.
- Buffer token-level `logprobs` in the streaming path and only emit `logprobs` in a chunk once the token is finalized; attach a `partial` flag for opt-in debug streams while keeping default behavior stable.
- Change streaming deltas for function/tool calls: we now emit argument fragments under `delta.function_call.arguments` and include `delta.function_call.name` only on the first delta; final chunk includes `finish_reason: \"function_call\"` and a synthesized `message` object compatible with non-streaming responses.
- Add a compatibility layer shim that maps Redwood internal role names to OpenAI roles (system/user/assistant/tool) and normalizes role for tool outputs so clients relying on role-based routing remain functional.
- Add extensive unit and integration tests: deterministic streaming harness, simulated network stalls, and fuzz cases for multi-token stop sequences.
- Observability: new metrics (compat.stop_triggers, streaming.partial_logprob_emits) and extra tracing on streaming sessions to aid post-deploy debugging.

Backwards-compat notes: default runtime behavior is backward-compatible for callers using standard non-streaming endpoints; streaming clients that rely on earlier partial-logprob behavior should opt into `streaming.debug_partial_logprobs=true`.

Tests and CI: initial CI runs flagged two flaky tests (streaming consumer timeout and linter fail on a generated file). Flaky tests were fixed by tightening timeouts and adding deterministic seeds; linter issues were fixed by regenerating the codegen stubs.

Checklist:
- [x] Normalize API boundary parsing and add parser unit tests
- [x] Stabilize streaming emitter and add harness tests
- [x] Add compatibility mapping for roles
- [x] Add integration tests against the openai-compat test harness
- [x] Update docs/compatibility and changelog
- [x] Add metrics and tracing hooks
- [x] Verified canary in staging with a subset of customers

b2d9e7f: streaming: buffer logprobs and gate final emission behind token finalize
c3e8a11: compat: stream delta shape for function calls; synthesize final message

changed_files: src/api/openai_compat/chat_handler.py — normalize_stop() added; previous logic accepted single stop string only. Example change: `stops = ensure_list(params.get('stop'))`
src/runtime/streaming_emitter.rs — buffer downstream_logprobs until token_finalized(); added `partial_logprob` feature flag and metric hooks
src/serving/function_call_emitter.go — emit delta.function_call.arguments fragments, attach name only on first chunk, final chunk emits synthesized message with content and finish_reason
src/sdk/python/openai_compat.py — updated streaming iterator to merge deltas into final Message and expose `partial_logprobs` opt-in param
tests/compat/test_streaming_tool_calls.py — new harness that simulates delayed TCP stream and validates final assembled function call message
tests/compat/test_stop_sequences.py — fuzz tests for multi-token stop across BytePair boundaries
docs/compatibility/openai_chat_parity.md — new section describing streaming vs non-streaming differences and migration notes
observability/metrics.yaml — add compat.stop_triggers and streaming.partial_logprob_emits counters
ci/pipelines/compat.yml — add streaming-harness job to run against the compat test matrix
tools/codegen/stubs/openai_compat_stub.py — regenerate stubs to reflect role mapping API
examples/compat/streaming_tool_example.py — added example showing incremental assembly of function call arguments
review_comments: Leah Kim: Left a couple suggestions on trimming logic when stop token crosses a token boundary — prefer deterministic tokenization-first trimming. Also flagged missing metric for stop hits.
Samir Patel (author): Addressed trimming with tokenization-first approach and added compat.stop_triggers metric. Updated tests to include cross-boundary stop cases.
Oliver Grant: Noted that partial logprobs feature could be abused for debugging; asked for opt-in flag and documentation. Also asked for explicit statement in docs about privacy implications.
Samir Patel: Added `streaming.debug_partial_logprobs` feature flag and documented privacy advisory in compatibility docs. Added e2e test that toggles the flag.
Priya Nair: Ran staging canary and reported one customer-specific regression with tool-name repeated across deltas; suggested dedupe on name emission. Fixed in commit c3e8a11.
CI: initial run had 2 failures (flake and linter); re-run passed after fixes.
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: consistent handling of `stop` for streaming and non-streaming calls
Stabilized streaming logprobs: default is now to emit only finalized token logprobs; opt-in partial emission available via feature flag
Better structured streaming for function/tool calls: incremental `delta.function_call.arguments` emission and final synthesized message to match non-streaming shape
Added observability metrics and deterministic streaming test harness
notes: Canary deployed to staging on 2024-11-20, internal canary traffic showed 0.2% delta in 99th pct latency (within acceptable bound). We flagged a follow-up to evaluate whether stop-sequence trimming can be done even earlier in tokenization (ENG-5012).
changelog_entry: 2024-11-21 — Unify streaming + non-streaming stop/logprobs semantics; stabilize function call streaming shape; add compat docs and tests
